Hi all —

Thanks for the details, Elena — helpful. Short explainer and recommended mapping below (keeps commercial clarity and minimizes surprise on invoice):

1) Responses endpoint (recommended modeling)
- Billing unit: Response Unit (RU). Each RU approximates a logical request and includes prompt+response. RUs are the primary SKU for new integrations.
- Token equivalence: we normalize RU to an estimated token bucket for pricing guidance (1 RU ~= 75 tokens for metering guidance), but invoices show RU consumption, not raw tokens.
- When to use: new integrations and workloads that treat each user action as one event (chat messages, search-ranking calls).

2) Chat Completions (Chat API compatibility layer)
- Billing unit: token-based meter (prompt+completion tokens billed). If you call via Chat Completions, we meter tokens directly (more granular).
- When to prefer: if you need token-level accounting for fine-grained cost optimizations (prefix caching, short prompts).

3) Legacy endpoints (older SDKs/endpoints)
- Billing unit: legacy token buckets (per-1K token buckets) and sometimes endpoint adapters that convert to RU-equivalent on the back end. For quoting, we avoid projecting legacy SKUs except for very specific backward-compatibility customers.

Pricing note (example rates for modeling only — final quote will be generated in our pricing system):
- Responses: 1 RU assumed = 75 tokens for modeling; list rate: $0.0024 per RU
- Chat (token-metered): $0.0011 per 100 tokens (prompt+completion)
- Legacy: $0.95 per 1K tokens (for reference only)

Example baseline (monthly, rough model) for Elena's numbers:
- Daily messages: 1,100,000 -> monthly ~33M messages
- If modeled as Responses: 33M RU * $0.0024 = $79,200/month (no discount)
- If modeled as Chat token-metered: 33M msgs * 150 tokens = 4.95B tokens -> 4.95M * $0.0011 = $5,445/month (note this shows the difference in unit semantics; token pricing example here is illustrative — the per-100-token and RU equivalence must be reviewed for fairness)

Important: the numbers above are only modeling heuristics. The big cause of divergence is how RU normalizes request cost and whether streaming/function calling splits across multiple RUs. For your traffic mix (10% streaming), expect ~5-8% variance depending on average response fragmentation.

Discount guidance for 12 months (illustrative bands):
- 0% commit: list rates above
- 20% commit: apply 20% off list (flat for hosted model) -> example Responses: ~$63,360/month
- Reserved/dedicated options: different economics; if you want reserved capacity we should model with Rishi on throughput SLO and SLA commitments.

Next steps I recommend:
- Ben: send the attached ratecard + this explainer to Elena as a friendly note and ask if they want a modeled quote in RU vs token view.
- Elena: tell us if you prefer invoice-level token reporting or invoice-level RU reporting (we can do both but prefer one canonical meter).

Happy to jump on a short call to walk the numbers.

—Lauren
